content.comment_body: Hello everyone, I'm a student and urgently need [product_name] to complete my exercises. However, I'm unable to install and use [product_name] on my Mac OS Catalina 10.15.4. Could anyone guide me on how to proceed or share any online resources for these exercises? I need to submit my homework soon, as required by my professor.

What kind of homework are you referring to? Do you need to download the application and transfer your program directly to hardware, or do you just need to send your program file for review? If it's only about writing and submitting the program file, you don't need the full version of [product_name]. The demo version allows you to write, simulate, and test your program before submitting.
@[user_name], the original poster can't install [product_name] version [version_no] on their Mac OS Catalina device, and that's the issue here.

Hi @[user_name], I understand the issue. The mention of 'exercise' and 'homework' made me think he doesn't have any hardware and might not require the full or latest [product_name]. The post didn't clarify why [product_name] version [version_no] specifically is needed, so I was trying to determine the necessity.

Hello @[user_name], In my view, the specific reason for wanting [product_name] version [version_no] is irrelevant. Many users have had repeated trouble installing [product_name] on current Mac or Linux systems, and [company_name] only supports operating systems it has officially tested. I hope he doesn't try installing the update from [company_name]'s website, as it's unlikely to work properly.
Hi, I'm also still waiting for a 64-bit MacOS (Catalina) compatible version. Is there any update about this? Thanks & Regards, [user_name]

I'm experiencing the same issue with Catalina, since it's been the default OS on Macs for a while now, and Big Sur has also been around for some time. Many MacBook Pros can't run earlier versions than Catalina. Should [company_name] remove Mac OS from its list of supported operating systems? It seems Mac OS is no longer properly supported. After all, it's a Java application, so mostly the installer for 64-bit systems is missing.

The issue with Mac OS Catalina is that Apple removed support for older 32-bit executables, as the OS has been mainly 64-bit for years. Users who previously installed [product_name] [version_no] on earlier versions can still run it; the problem lies in the 32-bit installer, while the program itself runs fine. It's similar to why some outdated or poorly maintained apps don't install on 64-bit Windows 10, which lacks the 16-bit subsystem.
I'm using Big Sur and attempting to install [product_name], but I only find upgrade packages, not the full version. Does anyone have suggestions?
Only upgrades and updates are available for download. To install these, you must already have the full version of [product_name] installed, which is only available for purchase.

analysis.insight_summary: Forum participants collectively report that installing [product_name] version [version_no] on MacOS Catalina is problematic because Apple's OS no longer supports 32-bit installers, although the software may work if previously installed. Users express frustration regarding the lack of a compatible installer and ambiguity over current MacOS support, especially since many new Apple devices can't revert to old versions.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect to install and use [product_name] version [version_no] on MacOS Catalina without complications, regardless of their computer model or OS version, and wish for an installer compatible with modern MacOS systems.
